messages:
maya: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a deterministic, route-aware probabilistic sampler for spans. Goal: predictable retention percentages per route + tenant tier, but deterministic so we can reproduce why a span was/wasn't kept. Thoughts?

jon: Nice. Determinism is huge for debugging. How are you planning to make it route-aware? fixed per-route rate or dynamic?

maya: Per-route base rate (from routing/config service) multiplied by a tenant-tier multiplier. We compute a stable hash from (route_id, tenant_id, trace_id_prefix) and compare against threshold. That keeps distribution stable and gives per-route control.

leila: Curious about trace_id_prefix — why not full trace id? collisions?

maya: Using prefix reduces cost of hashing and avoids bloating logs; plus we only need pseudo-randomness. We still include tenant and route to avoid cross-tenant coupling.

sam: Will this interact with head vs tail sampling? E.g., if we drop a head span but keep tail spans we'll break some tooling that assumes a root span present.

maya: Good call. Plan is: always force-keep the root span if route policy says keep X% of traces, then apply probabilistic keep for other spans using same deterministic decision per-trace. For tail sampling specifically, we add a last-chance selector that can override based on error signals.

jon: Is the deterministic decision per-trace or per-span? If per-trace it's easier for reconstructing traces.

maya: Per-trace — hash includes trace_id prefix so every span in that trace gets same decision, except for forced overrides (errors, latency SLO breaches).

leila: We should be explicit about exporter semantics. Some exporters dedupe or rely on root; others expect partial traces. We need to document a guarantee: if sampler keeps a trace, it will include the root span.

maya: Agreed. Will add in docs and console UI: "trace-level deterministic sampling with guaranteed root when kept."

sam: What about dynamic reweighting? If a route suddenly fires lots of traffic we might want to reduce sample rate. Can the deterministic approach support smoothly changing rates?

maya: Yes — we compute threshold = base_rate * tier_mul * route_overrides. Changing threshold affects which trace hashes fall below it — not stable across changes, but that's expected. We can provide a migration window (grace period) to avoid flipping too many traces at once.

jon: Could use a versioned seed to enable rollouts of new thresholds. E.g., seed=v1 then v2; console can show active seed for auditing.

maya: Exactly. Seed + timestamp in config. Also exposing seed in telemetry helps debugging.

leila: Ops question: where does this run? Collector side? In our sidecar?

maya: We prototyped it in the collector pipeline (before exporters) so it reduces downstream bandwidth and storage. Collector config will accept per-route policies from config service.

sam: A couple of edge cases: 1) multi-route traces (proxies) 2) sampled down but a later error should promote it (tail sampling). How do we promote deterministically?

maya: Promotion: if any span in a trace hits a promotion condition (5xx, error-tag, latency>threshold), mark trace "promote" and keep exporter-level decision to emit the rest. Implementation: maintain a small in-memory map of recently seen trace_ids flagged for promotion for X seconds.

jon: That's basically head+tail hybrid. Need to watch memory/time windows (we can't keep millions). Use bounded LRU + probabilistic TTL.

maya: Yep. We'll use a fixed-size cuckoo/LRU with soft TTL and metrics on eviction. Also add a fallback export policy: if map is full, emit a sampled set to a low-cost cold storage so we don't lose everything.

leila: Can we sketch the pseudo-code to review?

maya: Sure:``` 
# pseudo
key = sha1(f"{route}|{tenant}|{trace_id[:8]}|{seed}") % 100000
threshold = int(route_rate*tenant_mul*100000)
if key < threshold:
    keep_trace(trace_id, reason="route-tier-deterministic")
elif promotion_map.contains(trace_id):
    keep_trace(trace_id, reason="promoted")
else:
    drop_trace(trace_id)
```

sam: Looks good. A few notes: 1) keep the math in fixed-point to avoid FP drift 2) ensure seed rotation is recorded in metrics and trace attributes 3) tie console UI to show per-route effective sample rate and seed.

maya: Will do. Also plan to emit a span attribute when we keep/promo so debug tooling can filter: `redwood.sampler.reason`.

jon: How about evals / audits? We should periodically compute effective retention by route/tenant via downstream counters and surface regression alerts if it deviates beyond X%.

maya: Yep — we'll add a dashboard panel and an alert for >10% delta over a 1h window.

leila: One more: privacy/compliance — some tenants may require always-keep for compliance routes. We need hard excludes/includes in the policy.

maya: Policy supports hard-include/hard-exclude lists and overrides at tenant level. These are enforced before hashing.

infra-bot: deploy:collector/sampler v0.1 deployed to staging :rocket: (ci#2481)

sam: Great — can you post the staging link and a quick runbook for testing?

maya: Posted: https://ci.internal.redwood/job/2481 -> log + sample traces. Test plan in thread: 1) set route rate to 10% 2) send 10k traces across tenants 3) verify ~10% kept per-route in metrics + `redwood.sampler.reason` present.

jon: LGTM. Please add an RFC note for the seed + promotion TTL defaults and we'll move to canary in prod after a week in staging. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — will write up RFC and add console wireframes for per-route rate controls and seed history.

leila: Thanks, team.
